title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, Top Issues & Fixes
author: Ava Thompson
summary: Canonical playbook for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: standards, templates, SDK quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues with canonical fixes.
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines standards, templates, ownership, and operating procedures for Developer Experience documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. It is intended for DevEx engineers, technical writers, and on-call support engineers who author or maintain public and internal documentation.

Goals:
- Provide a consistent, high-quality developer experience across SDKs, quickstarts, and API examples.
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new users and internal teams.
- Ensure docs are discoverable, reviewed, and maintained with clear ownership.
- Maintain a canonical list of top support issues and fixes to accelerate support responses and reduce repeat incidents.

Scope:
- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java) including installation, authentication, and common patterns.
- Quickstarts & templates (Hello World, chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking).
- API examples (REST + SDK snippets, function calling, streaming, error handling).
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing flow, release tagging, quick rollback).
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage, diagnostics, KB entries).

Ownership and Roles:
- Doc owner: DevEx docs lead (primary contact for reviews and merges).
- Code owner: SDK team (responsible for code snippets and package releases).
- Reviewer pool: SDK engineers, SRE, security engineer.
- On-call support: referenced for urgent doc fixes affecting SLAs.

Standards and Style (required):
- Use concise headings and short introductory paragraph for every page.
- Add a "Why this matters" section for each quickstart.
- Include a one-line TL;DR at the top for long pages.
- Prefer examples that work out-of-the-box with the Redwood API sandbox token (or with environment variables).
- All code blocks must specify language (```python, ```bash).
- Add commands for installation, a minimal runnable example, and a troubleshooting section.
- Maintain consistent naming for endpoints and sample model names (e.g., redwood/assistant-v1).

Template Inventory (canonical files to keep in directory):
- sdk-guide-{lang}.md — language-specific guide (python, ts, go, java).
- quickstart-{use-case}-{lang}.md — focused hands-on tutorial (chat, embeddings, rerank, streaming).
- template-app-{use-case}.zip (or repo link) — minimal app template with README and tests.
- api-example-{feature}.md — REST and SDK examples for feature (streaming, function-calling, structured-output).
- docs-site-release-notes.md — internal tracking of site deployments and rollbacks.

SDK Quickstart Pattern (recommended page structure):
1. Title and TL;DR (1 sentence).
2. Why this matters (1 paragraph).
3. Prerequisites (account, API key, environment).
4. Install (package manager commands).
5. Minimal example (copy-paste runnable).
6. Deep-dive (explain parameters, options).
7. Troubleshooting (common errors + fixes).
8. Next steps & related pages.

Example Python quickstart (minimal snippet to include):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood/assistant-v1", prompt="Say hello in 3 words")
print(resp.text)
```
- Note: Always show how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY via export or .env; include example for Windows PowerShell.

API Examples (REST and SDK parity):
- Every feature page must include a REST curl example and at least one SDK example in a supported language.
- Include streaming examples (chunking) and function-calling examples with structured JSON output.

Example REST curl (streaming):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/assistant-v1","input":"Translate to French: Hello"}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publishing flow):
- Branching: docs/* for content changes; sdk/* for code samples.
- PR checklist (author must check): spelling, code blocks run locally, no secrets, tests updated when applicable, reviewers added.
- Staging preview: every PR triggers a preview build; confirm preview link prior to merge.
- Merge approval: at least one DevEx reviewer + one SDK engineer for code changes.
- Release: weekly deploy to production docs site on Wednesdays; emergency patches via hotfix branch.
- Rollback: use documentation site version manager to revert to previous deploy; file an incident in #docs-ops if rollback is performed.

Publishing Checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Title & TL;DR present
- [ ] Code blocks include language and pass linter tests
- [ ] Prereqs documented
- [ ] Related pages linked
- [ ] Reviewer assigned from reviewers list

Versioning & Release Notes:
- Tag major doc changes with vYYYY-MM-DD and list in docs-site-release-notes.md.
- Backport critical KB fixes to older pages if they are widely referenced.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current list):
1) Authentication errors (401/403) — canonical fixes:
   - Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY set and not expired.
   - Confirm token scope and project association in Console.
   - Show diagnostic curl with -v to inspect headers.
   - KB entry: "Fixing API key errors" (link).

2) Streaming responses incomplete / truncated:
   - Confirm client uses chunked transfer and handles streaming events.
   - Ensure request timeouts are above default (recommended 60s for long responses).
   - SRE check: tail inference runtime logs for dropped connections.
   - KB entry: "Troubleshooting streaming truncation".

3) High latency on specific endpoints:
   - Validate model selection vs. latency SLO. Recommend pinned lower-latency variant for real-time routes.
   - Check region routing and fallback policy (cross-region adds RTT).
   - Recommend client-side caching for repeated prompts (prefix caching).

4) SDK install/version mismatches:
   - Document exact dependency versions in quickstart and add a compatibility matrix.
   - Canonical fix: pip/ npm uninstall then reinstall pinned version; provide example commands.

5) Unexpected deterministic outputs or hallucinations during evals:
   - Advise adding temperature/top_p adjustments and deterministic flags.
   - Recommend running evals with latest vetted model; file regression if behavior deviates from baseline.

Canonical Fix Template (how to write a KB entry):
- Title: short and searchable.
- Symptom: text the user reports.
- Root cause: short analysis.
- Steps to reproduce: minimal commands or sample request.
- Fix/workaround: exact commands or config change.
- Owner & contacts: who to escalate to.
- Related pages & commits: links to PRs or patches.

Triage Playbook for Docs-Related Support Cases:
1. Confirm reproducible sample and redact secrets.
2. Reproduce using sandbox environment; collect request/response headers, timestamps, and any error codes.
3. If caused by documentation (outdated code sample, wrong flags), patch the doc immediately on docs/* branch, add label docs-hotfix, and notify #docs-ops and on-call.
4. If caused by SDK bug, open SDK issue, attach failing test, and add label sdk-docs-blocker.
5. If systemic (runtime or API), escalate to SRE and attach logs + correlation ids.

Monitoring & KPI for Documentation Health:
- Pages with preview build failures: target 0/week.
- Average time to merge doc PR: target <= 3 business days.
- Top support issues reoccurrence rate: target -20% YoY.
- Docs coverage for public SDK features: target 100% for GA features.

Maintenance Cadence and Review Process:
- Quarterly sweep: owners must review and mark pages as up-to-date or archival.
- Annual dependency check for code samples and SDK versions.
- Post-incident doc updates: required within 5 business days after incidents affecting docs content.

How to Contribute (quick steps):
1. Fork the docs repo or create a docs/* branch.
2. Add your change with the required template and update docs-site-release-notes.md.
3. Run local preview and unit tests (linter).
4. Create PR, add reviewers, and ensure preview link works.

Useful Templates (copy into new pages):
- Minimal Quickstart (markdown snippet).
- API Example with REST + SDK parity.
- Troubleshooting KB entry template.

Appendix A — Example Troubleshooting KB entry:
Title: "Fix: 401 Unauthorized when using SDK"
Symptom: SDK returns 401 on all requests.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY incorrectly or with surrounding quotes.
2. Run minimal generate request.
Fix:
- Export the key without quotes: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_XXXXX
- Confirm the key has not been rotated; check Console -> API Keys.
- Example diagnostic curl: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models
Owner: DevEx on-call

Appendix B — Example quickstart repo layout (text table):
- README.md — Overview and TL;DR
- example/{lang}/quickstart.{py,js,go} — minimal runnable code
- tests/ — unit tests for code samples (run in CI)
- LICENSE, package manifest

Related pages and references:
